ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The table lists four compounds and their formulas, molar masses, and boiling points. The molar mass of ethyl methyl ether is 60.10 g mol^-1, and the boiling point is 10.8°C; the molar mass of ethylmethylamine is 59.11 g mol^-1, and the boiling point is 36.7°C; the molar mass of propylamine (Propylamine) is 59.11 g mol^-1, and the boiling point is 47.8°C; the molar mass of trimethylamine is 59.11 g mol^-1, and the boiling point is 2.9°C. Reasoning: The molar masses of these compounds are almost the same, so the strength of intermolecular forces can be compared directly using the magnitudes of the boiling points. The one with the highest boiling point is Propylamine, 47.8°C, so it has the strongest intermolecular forces.
